children.title: Installing VPET GO
content: VPET GO is a fan-made color Digimon virtual pet built around off-the-shelf hardware and custom C++ software. Flashing the device is done with ESPConnect and the firmware binary distributed through the project release channels.

Before flashing, download and extract the latest firmware package. If the package includes rede.txt, it can be edited with your Wi-Fi SSID on the first line and password on the second line; this file is optional unless you plan to use online features.

In ESPConnect, set the baud rate to 2000000, connect the device by USB, open Flash Tools, download a flash backup, then select the firmware .bin with flash offset 0x0 and flash it. If the baud rate is unstable, lower it until the connection succeeds.

To add rede.txt, open LittleFS Tools, create a LittleFS backup, upload rede.txt to the filesystem root, save the partition back to flash, disconnect, and reset the device. A successful first boot presents CONTINUE or NEW DIGIMON.

children.title: Info
content: Info contains the main status screens for the active Digimon, including species, power, level, battle history, care stats, evolution hints, attribute, experience, battery, age, and weight.

children.title: Status
content: Status is composed of six sequential screens. Together they summarize the active Digimon: name, Stage, Type, probable Next evolution, Battles, Win Rate, Hunger, Strength, Effort, Age, Level, EXP, Power, evolution timer, Mistakes, and Weight.

Name identifies the Digimon species. Stage shows the current life stage. Type follows the Virus, Vaccine, Data, and Free matchup rules. Next indicates the most likely next evolution based on the current conditions.

Battles tracks fights across the Digimon lifespan, while Win Rate shows the percentage of battles won. Hunger and Strength naturally decrease over time and after battles, and can create care mistakes if left at 0 for too long.

Effort is increased by training and can influence evolution. Age, Level, EXP, and Power describe growth and battle readiness; levels can affect evolution and power, with Stage I capped at level 1, Stage II at 3, Stage III at 4, Stage IV at 6, Stage V at 8, and Stage VI at 10.

The evolution timer tracks progress toward the next evolution. Mistakes counts care mistakes during the current stage. Weight is measured in GB, increases when eating, decreases through fighting or training, and too much weight can cause sickness.

children.title: Album
content: Album shows a catalog of all Digimon from a selected Digi-Egg. Use A to move through catalog pages, B to select a Digimon and inspect its details, and A+B to exit the Album.

children.title: Care
content: Care covers daily maintenance: feeding, sleep, healing, and cleaning. Missed care can create mistakes, sickness, or injury, and those conditions can influence growth.

children.title: Food
content: Meat fills the Digimon Hunger hearts and is an infinite resource.
Protein fills the Digimon Strength hearts and is an unlimited resource. It also increases the Digimon weight.
There are additional items with varied effects.

children.title: Items description
content: Items that help with care and provide useful bonuses during the adventure. Use each one at the right time to keep your Digimon in good shape.

children.title: Special items description
content: Special items with unique effects can help in difficult moments or open new possibilities during your journey.

children.title: Sleep
content: Put your Digimon to sleep when it is tired to avoid care mistakes. Most features are unavailable while asleep. If the light is turned off and the Digimon stays awake, it is probably not tired.
Normal sleep does not stop the evolution timer. Deep Sleep puts the device itself to sleep and pauses the evolution timer while the system clock continues.

children.title: Heal
content: Heal removes sick and injured conditions. A Digimon may become sick from too much weight or accumulated poop, and may become injured after losing a fight.

children.title: Clean
content: Clean removes poop from the main screen. Letting poop accumulate can make your Digimon sick.

children.title: Digimon
content: The Digimon menu contains training, battle, quest, coliseum, cable battle, Bandai device battle, jogress, backup, and online actions.

children.title: Training
content: Training increases Strength hearts, and persisting through training also increases Effort hearts. Exercising makes the Digimon lose Weight.
Succeeding at the training minigame makes training more effective and rewards more Strength hearts.

children.title: Battle
content: Battle options include Quest, Colosseum, Cable Link, and VS Bandai. Quest clears areas through sets of fights, while Colosseum runs a sequence of Digimon battles.

children.title: Quest
content: Quest mode has 50 different areas. Each area contains three battles, and the third battle is always a boss fight.
Completing Quest battles can reward the player with items.

children.title: Coliseum
content: Coliseum mode runs a sequence of Digimon fights. Release 0.2a fixed a selection bug so opponents from Baby II through Ultimate can appear.

children.title: Cable Link
content: Cable Link connects physically to another VPET GO device for battles.

children.title: VS Bandai
content: VS Bandai connects with Bandai devices for battles.

children.title: Online
content: Online features are multiplayer resources that can be used with any other Tamer who has a VPET GO anywhere in the world. The only prerequisite is having a Wi-Fi connection.

children.title: Battle
content: Online Battle lets you battle against other Tamers. After selecting it, you must play the minigame for the currently selected Interaction mode, then choose between Create Room and Enter Room.
Create Room shows a four-digit number that you must share with the person you want to battle.
Enter Room asks you to enter the four-digit number received from another Tamer. Use A to change the digit value, and B to confirm and move to the next digit until all four are filled in.
If everything is done correctly, the battle starts shortly after.

children.title: Jogres
content: Online Jogress lets you connect with another Tamer to perform a Jogress. The flow is similar to Online Battle, but it does not require an Interaction minigame.
After selecting it, choose between Create Room and Enter Room.
Create Room shows a four-digit number that you must share with the person you want to Jogress with.
Enter Room asks you to enter the four-digit number received from another Tamer. Use A to change the digit value, and B to confirm and move to the next digit until all four are filled in.
If everything is done correctly and the Digimon are compatible, they perform a Jogress instead of a battle.

children.title: Trade
content: Online Trade lets two Tamers trade their active Digimon with each other. The flow is the same as Online Jogress, but instead of performing a Jogress, the Tamers exchange their active Digimon.
After selecting it, choose between Create Room and Enter Room.
Create Room shows a four-digit number that you must share with the person you want to trade with.
Enter Room asks you to enter the four-digit number received from another Tamer. Use A to change the digit value, and B to confirm and move to the next digit until all four are filled in.
If everything is done correctly, both Tamers trade their active Digimon with each other.

children.title: NacaStorage
content: NacaStorage has the Naca Upload and Naca Download options, which let you upload and download Digimon through the NacaTech website at https://battle.nacatech.es/.
Naca Upload sends your active Digimon from the device to NacaStorage. Naca Download sends a compatible Digimon from NacaStorage back to your VPET GO.

children.title: Store
content: Store lets you buy items or Digi-Eggs with acquired Bits. Press A to move through the available items, and press B to select one.
Press and hold A to exit the Store.

children.title: Options
content: Options include brightness, always-on display behavior, background selection, interaction mode, and Deep Sleep.

children.title: Brightness
content: Brightness sets the screen brightness.

children.title: Always On
content: Always On sets whether the screen stays on or turns off periodically.

children.title: Background
content: Background sets the backdrop shown behind your Digimon.

children.title: Wi-Fi
content: Wi-Fi contains the device network options: Quick Connect, Saved Networks, and Wi-Fi Off.

children.title: Quick Connect
content: Quick Connect shows a QR code so you can connect your phone to the VPET GO and then configure your Wi-Fi network.

children.title: Saved Networks
content: Saved Networks lists configured Wi-Fi networks. The device can save up to 5 networks at a time and switch between them.

children.title: Wi-Fi Off
content: Wi-Fi Off turns Wi-Fi off.

children.title: Battery Style
content: Battery Style lets you choose between 16 battery display models.

children.title: Sound Test
content: Sound Test lets you play the sounds used by VPET GO.

children.title: Interaction
content: Interaction sets the combat input style used during training and battles.

children.title: XAI
content: XAI rolls a 7-sided die before battle to determine the stop-bar speed. Lower numbers move faster; press B to stop the arrow at the highest point. Bar patterns can vary by Digimon.

children.title: Pendulum
content: Pendulum input asks you to shake the device until the screen color changes: blue for 2-6 shakes, yellow for 7-11, and red for 12 or more. Megahit colors vary by Digimon and are indicated by the Ready screen.

children.title: Deep Sleep
content: Deep Sleep puts the device itself to sleep and stops the evolution timer while the system clock continues. As of release 0.2a, it stays in Deep Sleep until you manually exit by pressing B.

children.title: Exit
content: Exit closes the current menu or returns to the previous screen.

children.title: Back
content: Back returns from the current menu. Because the software was originally written in Portuguese, some menus may show Voltar for Back and Vazio for Empty.
